sourcedFrom: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual (not printed on the cover)
cleanIntro: A Radical AR strips like any direct-impingement AR — two pins, carrier out the back, cam pin a quarter turn — and Radical's own book is unusually specific about two things worth carrying: the chamber brush gets five plunge strokes and three rotations, and nothing with wire bristles goes anywhere near the aluminium. The buffer is the part that will surprise you if you let it.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE — and the hammer must be cocked
steps.action: Set the safety selector to SAFE first. On an AR the selector will not go to SAFE unless the hammer is cocked, which is itself a useful check that the gun is in the state you think it is.
steps.quote: Set the safety selector lever to "SAFE". NOTE: The hammer must be cocked to place this firearm on "SAFE".
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — UNLOADING, p.24

steps.title: Magazine out before the charging handle moves
steps.action: Press the magazine catch and take the magazine out. Working the action first only strips a fresh round off a loaded magazine.
steps.quote: Press the magazine catch and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — UNLOADING, p.24

steps.title: Charging handle back, lock the bolt open
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear and push in the lower portion of the bolt catch to hold the carrier back. Any chambered round should come out as you do it.
steps.aside: KEEP YOUR FIREARM POINTING IN A SAFE DIRECTION. DO NOT TOUCH THE TRIGGER AND KEEP HANDS AWAY FROM THE EJECTION PORT.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to rear and push in lower portion of bolt catch.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — UNLOADING, p.24

steps.title: Eyes into the chamber through the ejection port
steps.action: Look — actually look — into the chamber. Radical puts this step in capitals in its own manual, and a bolt held back is not the same thing as a chamber you have seen.
steps.quote: LOOK INTO THE CHAMBER THROUGH THE EJECTION PORT TO MAKE SURE THE CHAMBER IS EMPTY.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — UNLOADING, p.25

steps.title: ⛔ Bolt carrier fully FORWARD before the receivers separate
steps.action: Let the carrier run forward before you touch the pins. With the carrier held to the rear the upper and lower will not come apart cleanly, and the book says so as a note of its own.
steps.quote: The Bolt Carrier Group must be in the full forward position in order to separate the Upper Receiver from the Lower Receiver.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — p.18

steps.title: Rear takedown pin, left to right, to its positive stop
steps.action: Press the pin from the left side of the lower and draw it out on the right until it stops. It is captive — it is meant to stop, not to come out.
steps.quote: hand side of lower receiver and pull the pin out on the right hand side of the receiver until it comes to a positive stop.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.29

steps.title: Pivot the lower down and away
steps.action: Hinge the lower open on the front pin. For most cleaning that is far enough — the carrier will come out with the receivers still hinged.
steps.quote: Pivot the lower receiver down and away from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.30

steps.title: Front pin too, if you want them fully apart
steps.action: Press the front takedown pin the same way, left to right, to its positive stop, and the two halves separate. Radical treats this as optional convenience rather than a required step.
steps.quote: If required for more convenience, completely separate the upper receiver from the lower receiver by pressing the front take down pin
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.30

steps.title: Carrier out, then the charging handle down and out
steps.action: Draw the charging handle back and pull the bolt carrier group out of the upper. Then take the charging handle rearward to its keyway and drop it down and out — it will not come straight back on its own.
steps.quote: Remove the charging handle by pulling it backwards the keyway and then down and out of the upper receiver.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.31

steps.title: Field strip complete — and Radical draws the line here
steps.action: Upper, lower, carrier group, charging handle. Anything past this is service work in Radical's own words.
steps.quote: IMPORTANT: Do not strip your firearm further than previously described.
steps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — p.34

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin — RIGHT to LEFT
deepSteps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin in from the right side of the carrier and pull it out on the left.
deepSteps.prose: Directional, and the book states the direction. Driving a stepped pin the wrong way is how it deforms in its hole.
deepSteps.quote: Push in the firing pin retaining pin from right to left of the bolt carrier group and remove the pin by pulling it out to the left.
deepSteps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.31

deepSteps.title: Tilt the bolt face UP and let the firing pin drop out
deepSteps.action: Turn the carrier so the bolt face points up, and the firing pin comes out of the back on its own.
deepSteps.prose: Gravity does this one. Shaking it or pulling on the pin risks bending the tip, which is the part that has to survive every primer strike.
deepSteps.quote: Tilt the bolt face up and remove the firing pin.
deepSteps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.32

deepSteps.title: Bolt in, cam pin a quarter turn, lift it out
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt into the carrier until it rotates and stops, turn the cam pin 90 degrees from its normal position, then lift it out.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt has to be pushed IN first — the cam pin will not clear its slot with the bolt extended, and forcing it there is how cam pins get sheared.
deepSteps.quote: Push the bolt in towards the carrier until bolt rotattes and comes to a stop, then turn the bolt cam pin through 90
deepSteps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.32

deepSteps.title: Bolt forward out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: With the cam pin out, draw the bolt forward and out.
deepSteps.prose: That is the carrier group in five pieces — carrier, bolt, cam pin, firing pin, retaining pin — and it is as far as it goes.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the bolt forward and remove it from the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.33

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Buffer — keep pressure on it, it is under spring tension
deepSteps.action: Depress the buffer and KEEP the pressure on while you press the buffer retainer pin. Then let the buffer and action spring come forward under control, depressing the hammer to let them clear.
deepSteps.prose: This is the part of an AR that launches across a room. The book names the reason explicitly — the buffer is under spring tension and will be ejected the moment the retainer is depressed if you are not holding it.
deepSteps.quote: Depress the buffer, maintaining pressure as the buffer is under spring tension, to prevent it from being ejected when the buffer retainer pin is depressed.
deepSteps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Stripping, p.33

deepSteps.title: Handguard — only if the gas block is coming off
deepSteps.action: Eight hex screws hold the rail to the barrel nut; with them out the rail pulls forward off the barrel.
deepSteps.prose: Radical's own note says not to bother unless you are replacing the gas block or gas tube. Routine cleaning does not need the rail off.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the 8 hex head screws that secure the rail to the barrel nut.
deepSteps.cite: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms — AR15 Instruction/Safety Manual — Handguard Removal, p.33

cleaning.name: BARREL — patches until clean, then decide
tasks: Patch from the CHAMBER end, one pass per patch, until it comes out clean
⛔ Keep the rod off the muzzle crown — that wear costs accuracy
Brass bore brush and solvent only if patches alone did not do it
Push the brush all the way through before reversing — reversing inside the bore sticks it
cleaning.quote: Avoid contact between the cleaning rod and the muzzle as resultant wear will greatly reduce accuracy.
cleaning.src: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms, Cleaning, p.36

cleaning.name: CHAMBER — five plunges and three rotations, specifically
tasks: A minimum of five plunge strokes
Then re-patch the bore, because chamber work pushes fouling into it
cleaning.quote: Use a minimum of five plunge strokes and three 360 clockwise, rotational strokes.
cleaning.src: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms, Cleaning, p.36

cleaning.name: CARRIER GROUP AND GAS TUBE AREA
tasks: Carbon off the bolt locking lugs, bolt rings and firing pin
Cam pin, extractor lip and the inside of the carrier
Around the gas tube where it enters the upper receiver
⛔ NO WIRE BRUSH on the aluminium — nylon or flannel only
cleaning.quote: clean all carbon and powder residue from around the gas tube in the upper receiver, bolt locking lugs, bolt rings, firing pin, bolt cam pin, lip of the extractor, and inside the bolt carrier group
cleaning.src: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms, Cleaning, p.37

cleaning.name: INSPECT, THEN OIL LIGHTLY
tasks: Wipe every component dry and look at it for wear, corrosion or damage
Anything found gets fixed before the rifle is fired again
One oiled flannel patch through the bore, leaving a film
Leave that film in place if the rifle is going into storage
cleaning.quote: Wipe all components clean and dry and inspect them for excessive wear, corrosion or mechanical damage.
cleaning.src: AR15 SEMI-AUTOMATIC INSTRUCTION / SAFETY MANUAL — Radical Firearms, Cleaning, p.37

reassembly: Reverse the strip: bolt into carrier, cam pin in and turned back square.
Firing pin in from the rear, then the retaining pin left to right — and check it is captured before anything else.
Action spring and buffer back into the receiver extension against spring pressure, retainer popping up to hold them.
Charging handle into its keyway, carrier group in behind it, both run forward.
Close the receivers and push both pins home.
⛔ Function check before the rifle leaves the bench.
fncheck: Magazine out, selector on SAFE with the hammer cocked. Look into the chamber through the ejection port. Charging handle back and released — the carrier should run into battery under spring pressure and lock. On SAFE, pull the trigger: nothing. Selector to FIRE: the hammer falls. Hold the trigger, cycle the charging handle, release the trigger and listen for the disconnector reset. ⛔ If the carrier does not fully seat, stop — on a DI gun that is usually carbon in the carrier or a cam pin fitted the wrong way round.
